task.name: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the model quarantines that model for the rest of the run
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2950
---
## What
Slice 3 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. When a provider refuses a dispatch before generating anything because the account may not call the selected model, that dispatch identity is quarantined for the remainder of the run: no later dispatch in that run reaches it, and the run continues on the remaining models. The availability classification (#2949) and the pre-dispatch empty-pool stop (#2950) are the earlier slices and have shipped; this one covers what the router learns *from* a refusal it did not predict.

Quarantine is enforced at the one dispatch seam every agent call already passes through (`run_agent`, where the configured-vs-resolved identity is stamped once per dispatch), not at each call site. Phases, roles and flows are covered because they dispatch through the seam, not because each was edited.

## Why
Availability resolution cannot be perfect: a provider may publish no catalog (unverified), the catalog may lag the provider's actual policy, or the answer may go stale mid-sprint. An explicit refusal is stronger evidence than any prior state. Without quarantine, a sprint meets the identical refusal once per story, paying WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan each time. That happened across four stories on 2026-09-04, and again three times on 2026-09-15 when the preflight decomposition assessment was routed to a withdrawn cheap-tier model in three consecutive runs. The existing transient-failure quarantine in `provider_health` is adjacent (reviewer-only, time-windowed, pattern-matched on capacity and rate-limit strings) and does not cover configuration refusals.

Two earlier attempts at this scope escalated in plan review after five plans each (sprint `1b75c9e1294c` on 2026-09-08 against this issue, and sprints `4186e8c6c16a` and `e4e1082e86bc` on 2026-09-15 against the parent #2914, which had been left open after decomposition). Every rejection asked for one more thing the criteria left silent: recognising every provider's refusal wording, surviving a process restart, covering one more dispatch surface. This revision names the one signal forge already classifies, states what happens to everything else, and bounds what "remainder of the run" must survive. The identity it quarantines is the canonical dispatch identity routing already uses (#2949), not a new one.

## Acceptance criteria
- The quarantine trigger is the pre-generation provider refusal the runner layer already classifies with its own structured failure code (shipped under #2913). A dispatch that ends in that outcome quarantines the canonical dispatch identity it was made with, the same identity #2949 resolves availability for, so that provider, transport, runner and endpoint scope are all retained. Quarantine applies whether that identity was previously available or unverified: the refusal converts unverified to unavailable for the rest of that run.
- A refusal the runner layer does not classify as pre-generation is never quarantined. It is logged with the dispatch identity and a bounded, redacted excerpt of the provider's response, sufficient to add a recogniser from the log line without reproducing the failure, and the run behaves exactly as it does today. Unclassified refusals fail open, never closed.
- Quarantine is recorded and enforced at the shared dispatch seam. A quarantined identity requested through the seam is refused before any provider call is made. The identity checked is the identity actually dispatched: when a runner substitutes a fallback model or transport internally, the substituted identity is checked the same way. A dispatch that reaches a provider without passing the seam is a bug in that dispatch and is out of scope here.
- Callers that are not a dev, review or validate phase are covered through the seam with no site-specific code. One test shows a quarantined identity is refused for a non-phase caller (the preflight decomposition assessment is the pinned case, since it is the one that halted three sprints).
- "Remainder of the run" means the lifetime of the sprint or run process that observed the refusal. A process restart within the same sprint may lose the quarantine, and after a restart the same identity may be refused at most once more before it is quarantined again. Persisting quarantine across restarts is not required, and the next run resolves availability afresh (#2949) rather than inheriting a quarantine that may no longer hold.
- A refusal of a quarantined identity is a routing outcome, not an agent failure. It carries a distinct marker so that transient-failure and retry classifiers in any phase never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability or adaptive profile history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.
- Every exclusion a quarantine causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it.
- The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend, naming the excluded models, where none do, the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
- The existing reviewer-only transient quarantine in `provider_health` keeps its current behaviour.

## Example
```
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  ✗ DEV   refused before generation — account may not call openai/gpt-5.4/cli under
          codex ChatGPT-account auth (HTTP 400). Quarantined for the rest of run 68aec168166d.
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.6-terra  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.51  5m 02s
  ... later story, same run, non-phase caller ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded for preflight decomposition assessment —
             quarantined after pre-generation refusal on issue-2775
  ▸ PREFLIGHT_DECOMPOSITION_ASSESSMENT   gpt-5.5
```

An unclassified refusal, left alone:

```
  ▸ REVIEW   some-model
  ✗ REVIEW   failed (HTTP 400, unclassified) — not quarantined; excerpt: "…model access
             requires organisation verification…" [redacted, 160 chars]
  (retry and classification proceed exactly as today)
```

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

options.consequence: Story is pulled from active work; a human re-examines whether the seam-based framing (single dispatch seam enforces quarantine) is achievable given per-runner refusal-shape heterogeneity, before any further dev cycles are spent.
options.evidence: Cycle 2 finding from anthropic-opus-cli: 'the production refusal this story was filed for... still classifies transient and quarantines nothing' — the motivating AC is unmet. New gaps surfaced each cycle (fallback quarantine bypass, resumed-run scope loss, API-loop HTTP 400 exception path, pooled-dispatch story-label loss, redaction) rather than repeats of the same bug, matching the whack-a-mole pattern the issue itself names from two prior plan-review escalations on this same scope.
options.risk: Story stays open and the underlying pain (repeated quarantine misses costing WORKSPACE/preflight/routing/plan spend across stories) persists until re-attempted.

options.consequence: Team ships a quarantine mechanism that doesn't quarantine the specific case that triggered the story, likely reopening this exact gap in a future run.
options.evidence: Substantial shipped surface (2599 insertions, 1318 test lines) and cycle-2 reviewer anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-cli gave APPROVE, crediting proper gating (NO_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE marker) and defensive logging; last gate result is PASS.
options.risk: Merges code where 3 of 4 reviewers still voted REQUEST_CHANGES and the pinned production scenario from the issue's own motivation remains unhandled — the exact repeated-spend problem the story exists to fix would continue unfixed for codex/ChatGPT-account refusals, plus known runtime bugs (quarantined DEV identity aborts the phase instead of rerouting to a remaining model).

advisory.rationale: This is the third escalation against this exact scope (two prior plan-review escalations on #2951/#2914, now a dev-review escalation), and cycle 2 found *more* new gaps (7) than cycle 1 fixed (4), including the pinned production case the issue was filed for (codex/ChatGPT HTTP 400 invalid_request_error) still classifying as transient and quarantining nothing — the enforcement surface (per-runner refusal classification) keeps growing new edge cases rather than converging.
